turns.message: lowkey question, what is the actual difference between a mono pressing and a fold-down stereo? I keep reading conflicting stuff and ngl I'm getting confused. is it the cutting head or the master tape or both??

good question Dev, both. mono uses a horizontal-only cutting head and a dedicated mono tape if one exists, fold-down is a stereo cut summed to mono playback. they sound different. the mono cut is louder and more present, the fold-down is just half a stereo. listening tests will show you, even without measurements.

planted_challenges.fact_value: thinks subjective listening tests are valid alongside measurements
planted_challenges.evidence_span: listening tests will show you, even without measurements

turns.message: Bram is right. I would add: even where measurements are clean, the sound character of a mono cut still differs in ways the measurements undersell. in my view this is one place where listening leads.

planted_challenges.evidence_span: the sound character of a mono cut still differs in ways the measurements undersell

turns.message: I would push back. The measurements undersell because the typical measurement set was designed for stereo. New measurement protocols catch what you describe. The conclusion is not that listening leads, it is that the measurement vocabulary needs updating.
